statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-53615 is an integer overflow in libblkid, the util-linux block device identification library, in util-linux 2.41.3 and earlier: parse_dos_extended() in libblkid/src/partitions/dos.c adds extended-partition start sectors in 32-bit arithmetic and does not apply the extended-area bounds check to the first two entries of each EBR, so a crafted DOS extended-partition disk image or removable medium that is probed can make libblkid report a false partition that overlaps the MBR. https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-h4rw-gv36-wmp5 lists 2.41.4 as the patched version; the fix is https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/05c2dbadf34cc74192287f377904afaaf4061623 in 2.41.4 (the same change is https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/a2d858176b609ab5b8535021a3af9cd302d23d31 in 2.42), which uses 64-bit arithmetic for the start sector, bounds-checks every EBR data entry and validates EBR links. The v2.41.5 tag contains that commit, and Debian lists trixie as fixed in util-linux 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-53615, Debian bug #1140197). The DHI util-linux packages from the 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 Debian source onward include the fix, as their shipped changelog shows (it also records widening the remaining DOS partition start and size variables in libblkid to 64 bits). The fixed version is the lowest such build still published. Builds made from Debian's earlier 2.41-5 source sort below it and are reported as affected.
